solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Diplomacy that actually changes things at the outset (4)

indicatorNotes.at the outset: each word's outset is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of that, actually, changes, things

annotation.surface: A remark that real-world diplomacy makes its difference early on.
annotation.walkthrough: The four words after the definition supply one letter each.
annotation.definitionFit: Tact is the diplomatic knack of handling people without offence.

entries.clue: Impressive article — our group very much entertained to begin with (7)

indicatorNotes.to begin with: take only what each word begins with

annotation.surface: A report that some gathering thoroughly enjoyed an impressive item.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very much' reads as one phrase; split it: 'very' gives SO, and 'much' joins 'entertained' to lose all but its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Awesome means inspiring awe, so impressive.

entries.clue: Describing group ignoring start of business hearing (5)

blocks.note: tribal describes a tribe, a group

annotation.surface: Someone summarises a meeting while skipping the opening business.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Describing group' asks for an adjective about a group: TRIBAL. The definition sits at the far end.
annotation.definitionFit: A legal sense: a case put before a judge in court is heard, and that process is its trial.

entries.clue: Dry arias broadcast — a mess! (8)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters scatter

annotation.surface: A critic judges a radio concert of dull opera songs a disaster.
annotation.walkthrough: The exclamation is the definition, not a comment on the broadcast.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: things in disarray are untidy and disordered.

entries.clue: Academic’s sign of approval on way up (3)

indicatorNotes.on way up: in a down clue, going up means reading bottom to top

annotation.surface: A lecturer's nod of approval helps someone's career rise.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': the academic is the reversed sign.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: a don is a fellow or tutor at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.

entries.clue: Guess specification you delivered after the expected time (9)

indicatorNotes.delivered: a word delivered in speech is judged by its sound
indicatorNotes.after: the next piece goes after those before it

blocks.note: the letter U is said like 'you'
arriving after the expected time is being late

annotation.surface: Someone guesses the spec they handed over was overdue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' pretends to mean handed over; here it means spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: To speculate is to guess without firm evidence.

entries.clue: Person in charge protecting street thief (7)

indicatorNotes.protecting: the outer word wraps round and protects the inner

annotation.surface: A local boss guarding a road against a robber.
annotation.walkthrough: The thief here is a particular kind, one who steals livestock.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific kind: rustlers steal cattle or horses from ranches.

entries.clue: Reptile, more miserable, losing head (5)

indicatorNotes.losing head: a word's head is its first letter, dropped

blocks.note: comparative of sad; its first letter S goes

annotation.surface: A snake sadder than ever after being decapitated.
annotation.walkthrough: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the adder is one species of snake.

entries.clue: Challenging attitude of French guy getting married (8)

blocks.note: a man engaged to be married

annotation.surface: A Frenchman about to wed has a combative manner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French guy' looks like one phrase for a Frenchman; split it after 'French'.
annotation.definitionFit: Defiance is an attitude of open challenge or resistance.

entries.clue: Mixer also dancing just a bit (4)

indicatorNotes.just a bit: only a part of the words is wanted

annotation.surface: A social gathering where someone also dances a little.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' pretends to be a party; it is a drink added to spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: Soda water is a mixer for spirits such as whisky.

entries.clue: Kitty’s circular route on return (4)

blocks.note: a loop brings you back where you started

annotation.surface: A cat named Kitty walks a round trip home.
annotation.walkthrough: Kitty is not a cat but a shared fund; the ’s means 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A kitty is a pool of money contributed by several people.

entries.clue: Sadly curses about pair of learners who could be having a row (8)

annotation.definition: who could be having a row

indicatorNotes.Sadly: letters treated sadly, badly, get jumbled
indicatorNotes.about: the anagram goes about the other letters

blocks.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate; two of them go inside

annotation.surface: Someone swears at two novice drivers, as if in a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'go', not 'cow': scullers row boats. The row that sounds like a quarrel is the misdirection.
annotation.definitionFit: Scullers propel boats with oars, so they could be having a row.

entries.clue: Tricky visit seen to need adjustment (9)

indicatorNotes.to need adjustment: the letters need adjusting into a new order

annotation.surface: A difficult trip that clearly needs rethinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' in the sense of delicate, as in a sensitive topic.
annotation.definitionFit: A sensitive matter is tricky, needing careful handling.

entries.clue: Yankee means to change sycophant (3,3)

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: An American intends to reform a flatterer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Means' reads as a verb, but it is only the letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A yes man agrees with everything the boss says, a sycophant.

entries.clue: Winning move securing popular English afternoon show (7)

indicatorNotes.securing: the outer word holds the inner one fast

blocks.note: checkmate wins a chess game; split MAT_E

annotation.surface: A decisive chess move and a popular English play in the afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Winning move' suggests sport or games generally; in crosswords it is usually the chess sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance at a theatre or cinema.

entries.clue: Once more a fuss principally about silence (6)

blocks.note: re means about, as in business letters

annotation.surface: Another row breaks out, mainly over keeping quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' is not a container here; it gives RE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: starting again from scratch means repeating the attempt.

entries.clue: First portion’s lead time? I’m not sure (7)

blocks.note: the lead in a film is its star

annotation.surface: Someone hesitates over when the first serving is due.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead time' reads as a planning term; split it into lead (STAR) and time (T).
annotation.definitionFit: A mealtime sense: the opening course, before the main, is the starter.

entries.clue: Separate two notes like some workers (4-4)

blocks.note: TI and ME from the sol-fa scale

annotation.surface: Advice to keep apart two memos, as some staff do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notes' are the sol-fa syllables do, re, mi (spelt me in crosswords), fa, so, la, ti.
annotation.definitionFit: Some workers are part-time, working fewer than full hours.

entries.clue: Reportedly permitted in a whisper? No (5)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is heard, so we go by sound

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether they were allowed to whisper, and is told no.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a question and answer: not in a whisper, so out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: Speaking aloud is the opposite of speaking in a whisper.

entries.clue: Card game photo (4)

blocks.note: a children's game of calling out matching cards

annotation.walkthrough: Snap is a children's card game where matching cards are called out.
annotation.definitionFit: Snap is both a card game and a casual photograph.

entries.clue: Absurd window feature — why you might say? (5)

indicatorNotes.you might say: said aloud, so we go by sound

blocks.note: the ledge at the base of a window
the letter Y is said like 'why'

annotation.surface: Someone asks why a window has such a ridiculous part.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Why' is not a question word here; spoken, it is the letter Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something foolish enough to laugh at.

entries.clue: Time unchanged after reflection (4)

indicatorNotes.unchanged after reflection: a word that reads the same when reversed

blocks.note: the answer reads the same both ways

annotation.surface: A moment that stays the same even when mirrored.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay only says the answer is a palindrome; the definition does the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: Noon is a time of day, twelve o'clock midday.

entries.clue: Rude mischievous child to lie outrageously (8)

indicatorNotes.outrageously: letters behaving outrageously are thrown about

blocks.note: an imp is a naughty child

annotation.surface: A cheeky child is told off for fibbing shamelessly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' is not a link word here; its letters belong to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Impolite means rude or bad-mannered.

entries.clue: Fondle cat, maybe (3)

blocks.note: a domestic animal, with cat as one example

annotation.surface: Someone strokes what may be a cat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that a cat is only one example of the second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the verb for stroking an animal, and the noun for a domestic animal such as a cat.

entries.clue: Supporter’s poster in this place extremely neat (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the letters at the extremes

blocks.note: first and last letters of neat

annotation.surface: A fan's poster, pinned up here very tidily.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely neat' reads as very tidy; it asks for the two ends of neat.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who adheres, sticks, to a cause or party backs it.

entries.clue: Thread story that goes on? (4)

annotation.surface: An online thread that tells a never-ending tale.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a yarn is a tale spun out at length, like thread.
annotation.definitionFit: Yarn is thread for knitting and also a long rambling story.
